class_evidence: 19 UCI/ELENA datasets, all run as two-class problems (Tables I-II, pp.1630-1631); only two-class problems considered (Sec. IV, p.1630); multiclass is future work (Sec. V, p.1641).
reduced_multiclass: One-vs-rest (e.g. Wine 1 vs 2+3, Vehicle van, Segment brickface, Letter Z vs A-Y), merged classes (Texture, Page_blocks) or two classes kept and the rest dropped (Abalone 18 vs 9, Yeast POX vs CYT) (Table II, p.1631).
smote_explanation: The generator is SMOTE's segment interpolation towards one of the seed's k2 nearest minority neighbours (Eq. 1, p.1626; Algorithm 1 step 5). In each boosting round, seeds are drawn with replacement from a ranking that weights each minority point by a logistic function of the number of majority points among its k1 neighbours (steps 2-4, Eqs. 2-3), so border points receive more synthetic samples. Generation is repeated in every AdaBoost.M2 round on a minority subset resampled by the boosting weights (steps 1, 6-10).
flags: Seed selection and Sample allocation are two sides of one weighted draw.

class_evidence: 13 datasets (Sec. 4.1, p.1827; Table 3, p.1828): 5 two-class (Hepatitis, BreastC, Haberman, CYTvsPOX, ME2vsOther) and 8 with all classes kept (Newthyroid 3, Balance 3, Saureus4 4, Anneal 5, Glass 6, Zoo 7, E. coli 8, Yeast 10). SSRBF and DSRBF run on all 13 (Table 4) with one softmax RBF network, no decomposition.
reduced_multiclass: CYTvsPOX and ME2vsOther are derived from Yeast (Sec. 4.1, p.1827).
multiclass_how: One class is oversampled at a time: SSRBF enlarges the currently smallest class J times before training; DSRBF pauses the memetic training at set generations and oversamples the class with the lowest sensitivity, each time by its original size (Secs. 3.3-3.4, pp.1825-1827).
smote_explanation: The generator is unchanged SMOTE: every original pattern of the chosen class is a seed joined to one of its k = 5 nearest same-class neighbours (Sec. 1, p.1821; Sec. 3.4, p.1826). What changes is which class is oversampled and how many times, set by class size (SSRBF) or by the lowest per-class sensitivity of the current best network (DSRBF). In DSRBF generation runs inside the training loop; SSRBF runs before training.
flags: Inside a pipeline applies only to DSRBF.

class_evidence: 30 synthetic two-class 2-D datasets (Sec. 4.1, pp.190-191) and 9 real datasets, each one minority class vs the rest, 8 from KEEL (Sec. 4.2, p.191; Table 1, p.192), with class or attribute noise added.
reduced_multiclass: Multiclass sources turned into two classes by joining one or more classes as positive and the rest as negative (Sec. 4.2, p.191), likely ecoli, newthyroid and cleveland.
smote_explanation: Generation is plain SMOTE with k = 5, oversampling to a 50/50 balance (Sec. 3.2, p.189). The only change is a filter applied afterwards: the Iterative-Partitioning Filter, an ensemble of C4.5 models on 9 partitions with majority voting, repeated until fewer than 1% of examples are removed in 3 rounds, which removes noisy original and synthetic examples of both classes (Sec. 3.1, pp.188-189; Sec. 3.3, p.190).
flags: Neighbours found with HVDM rather than Euclidean distance.

class_evidence: Drive PDF is the 2016 dissertation, Chapter 3 being the A-SUWO paper. Defined for binary problems (p.24; Sec. 3.5, p.46). 16 datasets, each a minority class vs the rest (Table 3.1, p.35); multiclass use only future work (Sec. 3.5, p.46).
reduced_multiclass: 12 multiclass sources reduced to named class(es) vs all other classes (e.g. Vehicle van, Ecoli pp, Glass 1, Segment WINDOW) (Table 3.1, p.35).
smote_explanation: Minority points are grouped by a complete-linkage clustering that will not merge two minority sub-clusters across a majority sub-cluster (Sec. 3.1, pp.26-28). Each sub-cluster's quota is proportional to its cross-validated classification error (Sec. 3.2, Eqs. 3.2-3.3), seeds are drawn with weights favouring closeness to the majority class (Sec. 3.3, Eqs. 3.4-3.9), and the partner is one of the seed's nearest neighbours in the same sub-cluster (Alg. 3.1, p.33). Placement stays uniform on the segment (Eq. 3.10).
flags: Page references are to the dissertation, not the ESWA article.

class_evidence: Set up for two classes only (Sec. 2, p.1624; Sec. 5, p.1629). 30 UCI datasets used as two-class problems (Sec. 4.1, p.1626; Table 1, p.1627).
reduced_multiclass: Multiclass datasets keep the smallest class as minority and merge the rest (Sec. 4.1, p.1626); which datasets is not stated.
smote_explanation: CGMOS keeps SMOTE's interpolation step unchanged (Sec. 2.3, p.1625). Seeds are drawn in proportion to a weight: the average relative change in kernel-density posterior certainty over all training points if a minority point were added at that seed (Eqs. 5-6, p.1625). Sec. 3 proves that the expected certainty gain is at least that of SMOTE on the training data (Theorem 1).

class_evidence: Read from the supplement only: the main PDF in Drive contains the INOS paper, not SMOM. 27 multiclass datasets, UCI and ordinal-regression benchmarks, all classes kept, with per-group minority and majority metrics (Supp. Tables S3-S10, S17-S20). No two-class experiment appears in the supplement.
multiclass_how: Each minority class is processed in turn against all other classes and oversampled until all classes have the same size (Supp. Sec. 7, Table S21); neighbours are searched over all classes; no decomposition or ensemble.
smote_explanation: SMOM keeps SMOTE-style interpolation between a seed and one of its k1 = 12 neighbours (Supp. Secs. 3, 5). For trapped instances, each neighbour direction gets a selection weight that penalises directions whose segment sphere contains instances of other classes (Algorithm S1; Supp. Sec. 3), so directions are drawn by weight rather than uniformly. NBDOS clustering decides which instances are outstanding (uniform directions) or trapped (weighted directions).
flags: Main PDF mislinked in Drive; placement law and allocation not confirmed from the main text.

class_evidence: 9 KEEL/UCI sets with all classes kept (3 to 6 classes; Table 1, p.13) and 2 sensor sets (Shuttle 7, Mafalda 3; Table 6, p.16). Only two-class data is a toy illustration (Fig. 3). In 5 of the 11 sets only one class is oversampled.
multiclass_how: Any class whose size ratio to the largest class is below the threshold is grown to N_max/IR (Eq. 1, p.4); each minority class gets its own ellipsoids fitted against all other classes (Eqs. 15-18).
smote_explanation: Each minority class is covered by Mahalanobis ellipsoids and its quota is split across them by inverse density times purity (Eqs. 32-34, p.11). In pure ellipsoids points are drawn along the ellipsoid axes without interpolation (Eqs. 37-40). In impure ellipsoids a modified Borderline-SMOTE interpolates: only borderline points are seeds, and the partner comes from their 5 Mahalanobis neighbours within the ellipsoid (Eqs. 41-42, p.12).
flags: Eq. 42 as printed points away from the partner (probable sign typo).

class_evidence: Targets binary tasks (Abstract; Sec. 2; Conclusion). 42 binary sets: 28 KEEL and 14 LibSVM (Sec. 4.1, Table 1, pp.9-10).
reduced_multiclass: KEEL x_vs_y and one-vs-rest splits of multiclass sources (Table 1); reduction not described.
smote_explanation: The partner is one of the k = 5 nearest majority instances (nearest enemies), found with a mix of Euclidean distance and how often earlier ensemble members disagree on the two points (Sec. 3.3, Eqs. 3-4, pp.6-7). The step is x + r(x_i - x) with r drawn from N(0,1), so points cluster near the seed and can fall on either side of it (Eq. 5, p.8). Generation runs inside every member of a sequential bagging ensemble (Secs. 3.1-3.4).
flags: Seed selection and per-seed allocation are not stated.

class_evidence: 19 two-class datasets (18 KEEL plus CM1; Table 2, Sec. 4.1, p.11) and two-class image demos (UTKFace; CIFAR-10 airplane vs rest; Sec. 6, p.14). Multiclass use only future work (Sec. 7, p.16).
reduced_multiclass: KEEL splits of multiclass UCI sources (Sec. 4.1, p.11); CIFAR-10 one-vs-rest.
smote_explanation: Seeds are only the densest d% of minority points, ranked by distance to their k-th minority neighbour, with d chosen automatically (Alg. 1, Sec. 3.1, pp.3-4). Instead of one random partner, the point moves step by step through all k nearest minority neighbours, each step bounded by the smallest majority-minority distance (Eq. 5, Alg. 2, Sec. 3.2, pp.6-8). A candidate is kept only if all its k nearest neighbours are minority points (Alg. 3, Sec. 3.3, p.8).
flags: Eq. 1 printed as extrapolation (probable sign typo).

class_evidence: Four 2-D simulated two-class sets (Sec. 5.1), 24 binary datasets from 16 UCI sources (Table 2, pp.34-35) and bearing-fault data with fault types against normal (Table 8, pp.44-45). Defined for one majority and one minority class (Eqs. 7-8, 24); multiclass is future work (Sec. 6).
reduced_multiclass: One-vs-others or class-vs-class (Abalone 16 vs 6, Yeast3-5) (Sec. 5.3; Table 2).
smote_explanation: Noisy or overlapped minority points inside the majority SVDD sphere are removed before generation (Secs. 4.1-4.2). Each remaining seed gets a number of points proportional to a weight combining closeness to the boundary and sparsity (Eqs. 21-24), and the partner is drawn from its 5 nearest neighbours in proportion to their weights (Eq. 25, p.25). Placement is SMOTE's; synthetic points that fall inside the SVDD boundary are rejected and regenerated, and any still missing are filled by copying the seed (Alg. steps 36-52, pp.26-27).
flags: Majority points outside the SVDD sphere are also removed before oversampling.

class_evidence: 21 multiclass UCI/KEEL datasets with 3 to 11 classes kept (Sec. 4.1, Table 1). One parameter-tuning run on Sonar (Fig. 7, p.2079) also reports GLOS results; the paper does not state Sonar's class count (two classes in the standard UCI version).
multiclass_how: Classes are labelled minority or majority by comparing their discreteness with the dataset-wide value (Eqs. 1, 2, 5); minority seeds are typed safe, borderline or small-disjunct and each type gets its own generator (MMO, AMBO, RRO) (Algs. 1-3).
smote_explanation: Only one of GLOS's three generators interpolates: AMBO, used for borderline seeds (Alg. 2, p.2076). Its partner is any instance inside a radius-R sphere, possibly of another class, and the step is capped at the seed's nearest-neighbour distance rather than covering the whole segment (Alg. 2 line 12). The number of points per seed comes from discreteness and is split across classes by their discreteness ratios. The other two generators place points on Mahalanobis contours (MMO) or at random within a radius (RRO).

class_evidence: 20 KEEL multiclass datasets with 3 to 10 classes kept (Sec. 5.1; Table 2, p.7) and 10 two-class KEEL datasets (D1-D10) in the validity check (Sec. 5.3, p.9; Table 6; Supp. Table 1).
reduced_multiclass: D1-D10 are KEEL two-class versions of multiclass sources (one-vs-rest such as Yeast4, Ecoli4; merged splits such as Ecoli-3-5 vs 0-6-7) (Supp. Table 1).
multiclass_how: One-versus-ensemble: classes sorted by size, each non-largest class oversampled against the original and synthetic data of all larger classes (Sec. 4.2.1; Fig. 4); afterwards inland samples of the overlap region are removed (Sec. 4.2.2).
smote_explanation: Clustering splits minority samples into inland, borderline and trapped (Sec. 3.2). Inland and borderline seeds are interpolated, inland ones with a partner from the same cluster and borderline ones with a nearby majority neighbour; trapped seeds get points from an optimised embedding, not interpolation (Sec. 3.3, Eqs. 2-4). The number of points per seed follows (1 - local density) times the class-size gap, categorical values come from a VDM-constrained set near the seed (Sec. 4.1), and borderline and trapped majority samples are removed afterwards.
flags: Core vs Partial debatable: trapped seeds (6-84% per dataset) are not interpolated. The binary and multiclass variants appear to be run on separate data.

class_evidence: OREM on 28 two-class UCI datasets (Sec. 4.1.1, Table 2, p.6174); OREM-M on 21 multiclass datasets with 3 to 10 classes kept (Sec. 4.2.1, Table 6, p.6177); OREMBoost on both (Sec. 4.3, Tables 10-11).
reduced_multiclass: 20 of OREM's 28 sets come from multiclass sources reduced to one or merged classes vs the rest (Table 2).
multiclass_how: OREM-M (Alg. 2, Sec. 3.2, p.6172): only classes with imbalance degree above 1.2 are oversampled; one point at a time, a class is drawn in proportion to its remaining quota, and a synthetic point is rejected if its nearest neighbour belongs to another minority class. Native multiclass, not OvO/OvR.
smote_explanation: OREM keeps every minority point as a seed with equal counts (Alg. 1). It replaces the k-NN partner set with 'assistant seeds' from a candidate region that grows until q = 5 consecutive majority points are met, keeping a candidate only if the sphere on the seed-candidate segment holds no majority point, so borderline majority points can be partners (Alg. 1; Sec. 3.1.2). The point is x_i + g(x_s - x_i) with g ~ U[0,1], halved when the partner is a majority point. OREM-M adds class-quota sampling and a nearest-neighbour rejection filter (Alg. 2), and OREMBoost runs the generator inside each AdaBoost.M2 round (Alg. 3).
flags: Variants: OREM is B, OREM-M is M, OREMBoost is BM; the paper is BM through OREMBoost and the union.

class_evidence: 20 multiclass UCI/KEEL datasets with 3 to 10 classes kept (Sec. 4.2, Table 2, p.7); 60 synthetic two-class datasets (Sec. 5.2, Fig. 5) and 50 more in the ablation (Sec. 5.4, Fig. 7).
multiclass_how: Membership to each class centre splits every class into safe, overlapping and noisy samples (Alg. 1); every class gets a quota N_max minus its overlap count (Alg. 2); cleaning goes through classes by descending size, treating all larger classes as majority (Alg. 4). No decomposition.
smote_explanation: Seeds are only the safe samples of each class, after membership-based noise removal (Alg. 1; Sec. 3). The partner is one of the 5 same-class neighbours among the safe and border samples, and placement is SMOTE's x_i + U(0,1)(x_j - x_i) (Alg. 2). Each seed gets a random number of points up to the class quota divided by the number of safe seeds. Afterwards, a CCR-style energy sphere moves overlapping and generated samples of larger classes towards their class centre (Algs. 3-4, p.6).
flags: Two-class evidence is synthetic data only. The post-generation step moves rather than deletes samples.

class_evidence: Binary labels only (Sec. 3.1, p.5). 37 binary KEEL datasets for evaluation, 5 KEEL datasets for tuning and 8 larger UCI datasets (Sec. 5.1, p.15; Tables 1-2). Multiclass is future work (Sec. 7, p.34).
reduced_multiclass: Multiclass sources made binary as smallest class vs rest (Sec. 5.1; Table 1 caption), e.g. Waveform, Statlog Landsat, Page Blocks, Letter; KEEL sets are ready-made binary versions.
smote_explanation: Anchors are drawn with replacement in proportion to a safety score, so each anchor gets a varying number of points (Eqs. 8-9, p.8). Two different minority neighbours of the anchor are drawn with weights from their clearance and a q-Gaussian locality kernel (Eqs. 10-11). The new point lies on the segment between those two neighbours, not between anchor and neighbour, with lambda drawn from a truncated q-Gaussian instead of U(0,1) (Eqs. 12-14, p.12). Nothing is removed afterwards. Running time is 39 times SMOTE's at the median (Sec. 6.7, p.29).
flags: The anchor is not an endpoint of the segment.

class_evidence: 30 binary UCI/KEEL datasets (group 1, Table 2) plus other two-class groups, and 5 multiclass UCI datasets (group 4, Table 5: yeast 10 classes, HR 3, employee 3, Drug200 4, MEDV 9) with results in Sec. 4.4.4 and Tables 15-18.
reduced_multiclass: Group 1 includes KEEL x_vs_y splits and one-vs-rest versions of multiclass sources (Table 2); reduction not described.
multiclass_how: On multiclass data the largest class is the majority and the smallest the minority (Sec. 4.4.4); SMOTE oversamples only the smallest class (Sec. 3.3); low-Loyalty samples are relabelled to the class with the highest Attraction before generation (Eq. 9, Sec. 3.2). Whether the middle classes stay in the data is read differently by two checks; only one class is ever oversampled, and results use binary metrics.
smote_explanation: Generation is plain SMOTE (k = 5) applied only to boundary minority samples whose Loyalty, an inverse-distance-weighted balance of same-class and other-class neighbours, lies between 0 and m (Sec. 3.3). Samples with negative Loyalty are treated as possible noise and kept out of generation, so the partner pool is also restricted. Afterwards Loyalty is recomputed: flagged minority samples still below 0 are removed and flagged majority samples are removed by an LOF test (Sec. 3.4, Eqs. 10-12).
flags: Category decision needed: only the smallest class is oversampled on multiclass data, scored with binary metrics.
